summary: Planeta CRATER is a strategy game for ages 7 to 12 set on an abandoned lunar base. As a life-support specialist, the player must bring the station back to life by managing four pillars: oxygen, housing, food and water, and energy. But the Moon is not Earth: with no atmosphere, little water, and a sky full of surprises, every decision must be rethought. Along the way, three major events put the base to the test: a solar radiation burst, a micrometeoroid shower, and an eclipse that cuts off solar power. Players learn that surviving on another world demands different choices and a different way of managing resources than life at home, and they discover what it truly takes to live beyond our planet.
details:
Planeta C.R.A.T.E.R

Project details

Planeta CRATER — a turn-based survival game where kids 7–12 run a lunar base by managing five life-support systems:

  • Living Habitat.
  • Oxygen Production.
  • Food Production.
  • Water Storage.
  • Energy Storage (solar panels + batteries).

Energy is the backbone — it’s what keeps oxygen, food, and water production running — so every day players choose where limited power goes, and something always goes without. Scripted events (a solar storm, a micrometeorite shower, an eclipse that cuts power) force real trade-off decisions, and random sub-events in between — a cracked panel, a clogged filter — mean players also pull resources from one system to repair another. There’s never a “safe” setup to settle into.

The numbers behind these events come from NASA and CSA data (NASA Open APIs) — solar activity, radiation readings, eclipse power loss, space food research — and the game labels each stat as “real data” or “game balance” so players always know which is which.

Simple language, icons, and color-coded bars make it readable for a 7-year-old with no prior space knowledge.
